references.text: The tribes of Reuben and Gad later confirm that they will not take an inheritance on the other side of the Jordan, which relates to their desire to remain on the east side.
The expression 'if I have found favor in your eyes' is also used by Jacob when he speaks to Esau, a common humble formula in requests.
Joseph gave his family property (אֲחֻזָּה) in Egypt, the same word used here for the land that Reuben and Gad desire as an inheritance.
Moses describes how the land east of the Jordan was given to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh as their inheritance.
Joshua reminds the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh of their obligation to help the other tribes before they can settle on the east side of the Jordan.
After the conquest of Canaan, the eastern tribes are allowed to return to their inheritance on the east side of the Jordan, as they requested here.
Israel asked for permission to pass through Sihon's land, but here Reuben and Gad ask not to have to cross the Jordan at all.
